findings.title: The new test uses a Go 1.21 builtin while the repository targets Go 1.20
findings.body: `min` is a predeclared builtin only starting with Go 1.21. This repository's Go 1.20 language version cannot compile either this use or the equivalent use on line 286, so `go test` fails before the cleanup tests run. Replace these with a local helper or explicit end-index calculation compatible with the supported toolchain.

findings.title: Configured batch sizes can exceed database bind-parameter limits
findings.body: The non-SQLite path creates one bind placeholder for every fetched ID, with no chunking or limit enforcement. A configured cleanup batch above 65,535 IDs causes MySQL/PostgreSQL prepared statements to fail due to their parameter-count limits; the same cleanup then retries and fails every cycle. The previous subquery-based delete did not consume one bind parameter per row. Split deletes into backend-safe chunks or validate the configuration against the supported limit.

findings.title: SQLite large-batch SQL construction is quadratic
findings.body: For SQLite batches over 999, each loop iteration formats a new string containing the entire accumulated ID list. This repeatedly copies the growing list, making construction O(n²) in both allocation and copy work. The newly added test configures a 32,767-item batch, and production batches of that size can spend substantial time and memory in this loop before issuing the delete. Build the list with a strings.Builder/byte buffer or delete in bounded chunks.

findings.title: Successful cleanup batches are logged as errors with every selected ID
findings.body: This log statement is reached only after `fetchIDs` succeeded, so `err` is nil, yet it emits an Error log containing the complete ID slice. The same pattern occurs for the post-delete, max-count, and orphan-tag paths. Normal cleanup therefore produces error-level events and serializes up to an entire configured batch of IDs twice per batch, causing misleading alerting and potentially very large log ingestion during a backlog. Use an appropriate non-error level and log counts rather than full ID lists.

findings.title: The change increases the cadence of every cleanup job by tenfold
findings.body: Changing the shared cleanup ticker from ten minutes to one minute does not only retry annotation cleanup; it also runs snapshot deletion, dashboard-version deletion, image cleanup, invite expiration, short-URL cleanup, and query-history row-limit enforcement ten times as often. If a run lasts longer than a minute, the ticker also leaves a pending tick, allowing another full run to start immediately after it finishes. This substantially increases background database work for unrelated services; retain the existing global cadence and schedule any needed annotation retry separately.
